fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,

paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Mara at the counter said the center called just after eight on Thursday and added six trays to the original order. The paper copy is clipped to the blue board, and the scanned copy is in the folder marked Harbor Friday. I am dictating the notes while Jonah checks the labels, so the team has the same details before the first delivery leaves.

Well, the order has been on the calendar since Monday, and the first version asked for four trays of lemon buns and three trays of seeded rolls. The caller added two trays of plain rolls and two trays of apricot hand pies on Thursday, but kept the original delivery window. The Harbor Arts Center is holding a volunteer breakfast in its second-floor gallery, and the service lift is narrow, so the cartons must fit through the east entrance. The main entrance has a stone step and cannot be used for the loaded trolley. The order form says delivery at nine forty-five, and the driver needs to ring the gallery bell rather than the street doorbell.

I checked the counter copy against the message from Mara, and the total is eleven trays across four kinds of baking. The lemon buns use the pale yellow label, and the seeded rolls use the brown label with the small wheat picture. The plain rolls have a green label, and the apricot hand pies have an orange label with no allergy mark because the filling is fruit. The center asked us to keep the labels on the short side of each tray, so they can read them when the boxes are stacked. The labels are already printed, but the plain roll sheet has eight labels left, and that is enough for this order plus the next small batch.

The numbered section on the order form has the packing details:
1. Put the two apricot trays in separate shallow cartons because the crusts break if a heavy tray is set above them.
2. Stack the lemon bun trays together with the printed count facing the aisle.
3. Keep the seeded rolls in the carton marked for the gallery table.
4. Place the plain rolls beside the seeded rolls, but do not put either roll carton under the pie cartons.
5. Add one paper menu to the top carton and leave the invoice in the clear sleeve attached to the outside. The menu lists the ingredients, and the invoice lists the balance due of eighty-six dollars. The center paid a thirty-dollar deposit at the time of the first call.

Jonah has reserved the east cooler shelf for the order because the cream cakes for the morning display take up the lower shelf. The trays should stay covered until the driver comes back from the market run, and the packing room stays cooler than the front counter during the late morning. We had a warm spell last week, and the glaze on another order went soft before noon, so the shift lead asked us to watch the room thermometer today. If the packing room reaches seventy-two degrees before the driver returns from the market run, move the covered trays to the walk-in cooler and write the time on the form. If the room stays below that mark, leave the trays on the reserved shelf.

The caller was careful about the entrance and said, “Please use the east entrance by the mural because our caretaker will keep that door open until ten.” The caretaker is named Luis, and he will be near the gallery stairs with a folding cart. The driver should call the bakery if Luis is not there at nine forty-five and should not leave the boxes outside the entrance. The center has a morning class in the lobby, so the driver must not block the ramp while bringing in the trolley. The ramp stays clear for visitors and for the cleaning cart that passes every few minutes.

There is a note on the back of the form about the return containers. The center is borrowing three blue bread crates and one low tray for the pies, and Luis will send them back with our driver after the breakfast. The blue crates have white tags with the bakery phone number, and the low tray has a small crack near one corner, so it should travel flat. The tags are not price labels and must stay attached until the crates reach the shop. The driver can bring the returned crates through the side entrance in the afternoon, but the side entrance is locked after four, and the evening staff do not have the outside key.

I have forwarded the order form now, and the scan went to the packing room folder and to the driver tablet. Jonah has the printed copy by the scale, and Mara has kept the call note at the counter in case the center rings again. The delivery total remains eleven trays, and the window remains nine forty-five. The deposit is recorded, and the balance is still eighty-six dollars. The shift lead will compare the packed cartons with the numbered section before they go on the trolley, and the form should travel in its clear sleeve with the invoice visible.

At the end of the shift, the driver should note whether all three blue crates and the low pie tray came back and bring the returned containers to the wash bench rather than stacking them beside the clean cartons. If Luis needs another day to return anything, the driver should write down which container is missing and tell Mara when he gets back. The blue crates belong to the bakery, and the cracked low tray is still usable as long as it stays flat on the trolley. The final delivery check is the east entrance, the gallery bell, the clear ramp, and the covered trays kept under the stated temperature condition."}]
